'''Włodzimierz Marek Tulczyjew''' (18 June 1931 – 4 December 2022) was a [[Polish people|Polish]]-[[Italians|Italian]] [[physicist]] and [[mathematician]], known for his contributions to the geometric formulation of classical mechanics and [[Field (physics)|field theory]]. He was a professor emeritus of mathematical methods of physics at the [[University of Camerino]] and a member of the Academy of Sciences of [[Turin]].<ref name=":1">{{cite web | url=https://umi.dm.unibo.it/2023/01/04/wlodzimierz-marek-tulczyjew-1931-2022/ | title=Włodzimierz Marek Tulczyjew (1931 - 2022) | date=4 January 2023 }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite web | url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=114106 | title=Wlodzimierz Tulczyjew - the Mathematics Genealogy Project }}</ref><ref name=":3">{{cite web | url=https://www.accademiadellescienze.it/accademia/soci/wlodzimierz-marek-tulczyjew | title=Accademia delle Scienze }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite web | url=https://zbmath.org/authors/?q=tulczyjew | title=Włodzimierz Marek Tulczyjew - Author Profile - zbMATH Open }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Tulczyjew was born in [[Włodawa]], a small town in eastern [[Poland]], in 1931. From 1933 to 1943, he lived in Ostrów Lubelski, where his father worked as an accountant. In 1943, he was deported with his family to Germany, where he worked in an armaments factory. In June 1945, he returned to Lublin. Later on he moved to Warsaw where, in 1952, he graduated with a diploma from the State Telecommunication Technical School.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=Urbański |first=Paweł |date=2023 |title=Włodzimierz Marek Tulczyjew (1931-2022) |url=http://yadda.icm.edu.pl/baztech/element/bwmeta1.element.baztech-43809b96-5b51-485c-a7d0-87f6ced85a22 |journal=Postępy Fizyki |language=PL |volume=T. 74, z. 4 |issn=0032-5430}}</ref>

From 1952 to 1956, he studied in the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics at the [[University of Warsaw]].  During his studies, Tulczyjew joined a group centered around [[Leopold Infeld]] ([[Jerzy Plebański]], [[Andrzej Trautman]], [[Iwo Białynicki-Birula]], Stanisław Bażański, and others). He obtained his Ph.D. in 1959 and his D.Sc. in 1965 at the [[University of Warsaw]] under the supervision of Andrzej Trautman.<ref name=":2" /> Then he became an assistant professor there. Tulczyjew's research was highly valued by Infeld, who, in his posthumously published memoirs, referred to Włodek as his most outstanding student.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Trautman |first1=Andrzej |last2=Salisbury |first2=Donald |date=26 December 2019 |title=Memories of my early career in relativity physics |volume=44 |issue=4–5 |pages=391–413 |doi=10.1140/epjh/e2019-100044-5 |journal=The European Physical Journal H|arxiv=1909.12165 }}</ref> After Infeld's death (January 15, 1968), Tulczyjew decided to emigrate. He left Poland on September 28, 1968, and through Rome reached Canada, at the University of Calgary.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4" />

In the late 1980s, Tulczyjew took early retirement in Canada and relocated to Camerino, Italy. He was appointed as a professor ''per chiara fama'' (a distinguished position) of Mathematical Methods of Physics at the University of Camerino. He soon began collaborating with Giuseppe Marmo, a professor at Federico II University in Naples, and with the National Institute of Nuclear Physics.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />

In the 2000s, he initiated new collaborations with scholars at the University of Bari, including Fiorella Barone and Margherita Barile, and mentored a PhD student, Antonio De Nicola.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" />

He retired in 2006, but remained active in research and teaching until his death in 2022.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4" />

== Scientific work ==
Tulczyjew's main research interest was the geometry of [[classical mechanics]] and field theory, especially the symplectic and multisymplectic structures that underlie the Hamiltonian and [[Lagrangian formulations]], and the Legendre transformation that connects them. Among his notable contributions are the Tulczyjew triple, the Tulczyjew symplectic structure, the Tulczyjew-Dedecker differential, and the Tulczyjew isomorphism. He also worked on [[general relativity]], gauge theories, [[quantum mechanics]], and differential geometry.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />

In his habilitation thesis, Tulczyjew presented a scheme of relativistic quantum mechanics as a scattering theory, where antiparticles are described as particles moving backward in time. His work prefigured geometric quantization, later developed  by Jean-Marie Souriau and Bertram Kostant. Tulczyjew was also one of the first to recognize the relationship between Utiyama's theory and Yang-Mills field theory. Seeking the proper formulation of relativistic quantum mechanics led him back to the foundations of classical theories, especially to classical mechanics and the fundamentals of variational calculus (or rather the variational description of physical systems).<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4" />

Tulczyjew's approach to relativistic quantum mechanics led him to revisit the foundations of classical mechanics and the variational calculus, where he sought a geometric formulation. His work inspired several colleagues, particularly at the University of Warsaw, to explore multisymplectic geometry and its applications in variational calculus. Notable collaborators include Jerzy Kijowski, Wiktor Szczyrba, Jacek Komorowski, and Krzysztof Gawędzki.<ref name=":0" />

During his time in Canada, Tulczyjew continued to work on the dynamics of charged particles and the inverse problem of variational calculus, which seeks the conditions for a system of partial differential equations to be derived from a Lagrangian. He solved this problem by constructing a double variational complex and proving Poincaré's Lemma for this structure. His work was highly regarded by contemporaries such as [[André Lichnerowicz]], [[Alexandre Mikhailovich Vinogradov|Alexandre Vinogradov]], [[Paul Dedecker]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Tulczyjew |first=W. M. |chapter=The Euler-Lagrange resolution |date=1980 |editor-last=García |editor-first=P. L. |editor2-last=Pérez-Rendón |editor2-first=A. |editor3-last=Souriau |editor3-first=J. M. |title=Differential Geometrical Methods in Mathematical Physics |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/BFb0089725 |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |volume=836 |language=en |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |pages=22–48 |doi=10.1007/BFb0089725 |isbn=978-3-540-38405-2}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Dedecker |first1=P. |chapter=Spectral sequences and the inverse problem of the calculus of variations |date=1980 |title=Differential Geometrical Methods in Mathematical Physics |volume=836 |pages=498–503 |editor-last=García |editor-first=P. L. |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/BFb0089761 |access-date=2024-07-22 |place=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg |doi=10.1007/bfb0089761 |isbn=978-3-540-10275-5 |last2=Tulczyjew |first2=W. M. |editor2-last=Pérez-Rendón |editor2-first=A. |editor3-last=Souriau |editor3-first=J. M.}}</ref> Ian Anderson attributed the discovery of the variational bicomplex to both Tulczyjew and Vinogradov independently.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Mathematical aspects of classical field theory: proceedings of the AMS-IMS-SIAM Joint Summer Research Conference held July 20 - 26, 1991, with support from the National Science Foundation |date=1992 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |isbn=978-0-8218-5144-9 |editor-last=Gotay |editor-first=Mark J. |series=Contemporary mathematics |location=Providence, RI |editor-last2=Marsden |editor-first2=Jerrold E. |editor-last3=Moncrief |editor-first3=Vincent |editor-last4=American Mathematical Society |editor-last5=Institute of Mathematical Statistics |editor-last6=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics}}</ref>

In 1974, Tulczyjew published a seminal paper on Hamiltonian and Lagrangian systems,<ref>{{Cite web |title=MathSciNet |url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=MR0388451 |access-date=2024-07-22 |website=mathscinet.ams.org}}</ref> providing a full geometric interpretation of the Legendre transformation.<ref>{{cite arXiv |eprint=math-ph/9909029 |first1=Wlodzimierz M. |last1=Tulczyjew |first2=Pawel |last2=Urbanski |title=A slow and careful Legendre transformation for singular Lagrangians |date=1999-09-27}}</ref> Later on, Tulczyjew formulated his innovative vision of variational principles in physics by providing a conceptual framework.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tulczyjew |first=Włodzimierz M. |date=2003 |title=The origin of variational principles |url=https://eudml.org/doc/282004 |journal=Banach Center Publications |volume=59 |issue=1 |pages=41–75 |issn=0137-6934}}</ref> The basic geometric structure associated with the Legendre transformation is now known as the Tulczyjew triple. Among his contributions to mathematical physics, Tulczyjew, in collaboration with Maria Rosa Menzio, developed an approach linking Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics via symplectic structures, involving the Tulczyjew map.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Menzio
 | first1 = Maria Rosa
 | last2 = Tulczyjew
 | first2 = Włodzimierz Marek
 | title = Infinitesimal symplectic relations and generalized Hamiltonian dynamics
 | journal = Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré, Section A
 | volume = 28
 | issue = 3
 | year = 1978
 | pages = 349–367
}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{cite journal |last1=Grabowska |first1=Katarzyna |last2=Grabowski |first2=Janusz |year=2013 |title=Tulczyjew triples: From statics to field theory |journal=Journal of Geometric Mechanics |volume=5 |pages=445–476 |doi=10.3934/jgm.2013.5.445 |number=4|arxiv=1306.2744 }}</ref> Tulczyjew's contributions were recognized internationally, and in 1981, he was elected as a foreign member of the Accademia delle Scienze di Torino.<ref name=":3" />

Tulczyjew published around 100 [[scientific paper]]s and several books, including A symplectic framework for field theories (1979), and Geometric Formulation of Physical Theories (1989). He collaborated with many distinguished mathematicians and physicists.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/2276177 |access-date=2024-07-13 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Tulczyjew was elected as a member of several academies and societies, such as:<ref name=":3" />
* The [[Academy of Sciences of Turin]] (1981).<ref name=":3" />
* The Polish Academy of Sciences (1990).<ref name=":4" />
* The Gold Cross of Merit awarded by the President of Poland (2014).<ref name=":4" />
